title: Late Breaking Results: TriSC: Low-Cost Design of Trigonometric Functions with Quasi Stochastic Computing
problem: Low-cost and hardware-efficient design of trigonometric functions is challenging. Existing stochastic computing implementations overlook the importance of data converters and bit-stream generators, requiring designs that efficiently handle both the computation circuit and decorrelation of bit-streams for non-linear functions.
motivation: Trigonometric functions are computation-intensive and demanded by energy-critical applications like image transformation and robotic control, making low-cost hardware implementations essential.
method: TriSC uses quasi-random bit-streams to compute trigonometric functions via stochastic computing without delay elements. The design co-optimizes the computation circuit and bit-stream generator, leveraging state-of-the-art quasi-random generators to achieve decorrelation while improving accuracy.
key_novelty: TriSC eliminates delay elements required in existing stochastic computing trigonometric designs while achieving state-of-the-art accuracy through quasi-random bit-stream generation.
contributions: Novel SC-based trigonometric function design using quasi-random bit-stream generators
Elimination of delay elements while improving output accuracy versus existing SC designs
Demonstration of 92% energy savings compared to state-of-the-art SC trigonometric implementations
First SC applications to 2D image transformation and robotic arm forward kinematics
limitations: Specific hardware implementation details, scalability analysis, and comparison against conventional implementations not discussed.
primary_theme: low-cost stochastic computing for trigonometric functions
